title: Godot 4 Tween node removal and kill/re-create

blocks.text:
After migrating a Godot 3.x project to Godot 4, you see errors like
Invalid call. Nonexistent function 'interpolate_property' in base 'Tween'
or Cannot find class "Tween" as a node type. If you had Tween nodes in
your scene tree, they may have been silently removed during the conversion
process. Scripts that reference $Tween fail with null access errors.

Godot 4 completely replaced the Tween system. In Godot 3, Tween was a node
you added to the scene tree, configured with interpolate_property() and
started with start(). In Godot 4, the Tween node no longer exists. Instead,
tweens are lightweight objects created procedurally with create_tween().
Every part of the old API changed: the node reference is gone,
interpolate_property() was replaced by tween_property(), and you do not
call start() because tweens start automatically upon creation. Property
names also changed (rect_position → position, rect_scale → scale); if an
old tween targeted these renamed properties, it silently does nothing even
when the syntax is correct.

# Godot 3 — the old way (no longer works)
var tween = $Tween
tween.interpolate_property(
  self, "modulate:a",
  0.0, 1.0, 0.5,
  Tween.TRANS_SINE, Tween.EASE_IN_OUT
)
tween.start()

Godot 4 tweens are one-shot by default. For tweens that need to restart —
like a button hover that plays every time the mouse enters — kill the old
tween and create a new one. Killing and recreating guarantees a clean
slate; restarting a running tween in Godot 3 could produce unexpected
intermediate states.
